title.narrative: Universal Rights Group: Support journalist engagement at the Human Rights Council: improving transparency, visibility and public accountability

description.narrative: Build the capacity (knowledge, expertise and skills) of media professionals/journalists from developing countries, as key human rights defenders in their countries and regions; and increase awareness and knowledge of, and interest in, the Human Rights Council and its work among rights-holders around the world, thereby improving transparency, visibility and public accountability.

title.narrative: Empower journalists and other media professionals, especially in developing countries, as key human rights defenders, so that they are better able to hold governments accountable against the State’s international human rights obligations and commitments.
Increase in the number and quality of articles/broadcasts focused on the work and output of the Human Rights Council.

target.value: An increase is documented in the number (as well as the quality) of articles and broadcasts about the HRC from journalists who participated in the programme.

actual.value: 117 articles were published by the programme participants raising awareness about the human rights mechanisms, HRC session they had attended, as well as interviews with diplomats and OHCHR representatives, which they had conducted during the programme. Although the total number fell short of the ambitious target of 3 articles per session per each participant, the programme did contribute to the visibility of the Council as well as raised the participants' technical understanding thereof.

title.narrative: Improved levels of media coverage, especially in developing countries (and especially in Africa) featuring or about the Human Rights Council and the wider UN human rights system.

target.value: Each journalist in the programme will produce a minimum of three articles; A measurable increase in media coverage in the UN HRC and its work can be observed.

actual.value: 16 articles were published during this session.
